text.p: Belgian electronics company Barco NV raised on Wednesday its 1997 profit forecast after bettering its 1996 targets.

"Last September we said we expected net current profit to rise between 10 and 15 percent from internal growth. Now we are expecting 15 percent internal growth," chief executive officer Hugo Vandamme told a news conference.

Vandamme did not rule out additional, external growth, noting Barco had around five billion Belgian francs in cash. "We are working on lots of aquisitions. We cannot say if they will be in a few months...or next year. We are very careful," he said
Barco said 1996 net current earnings rose 31 percent to 2.795 billion Belgian francs. At the presentation of half-year results last September the group had said it was tabling on a 25 percent rise.

Earnings per share rose 14 percent to 229 francs and Barco said it would propose a 24 percent rise in its gross dividend to 62 francs a share, noting its number of shares had risen 15 percent to 12,203,840, due mainly to the expiry of warrants.
Vandamme said earnings growth came in all markets, although as a proportion of turnover the importance of the Americas and Asia grew, while that of Europe fell.

Barco turnover rose 25.5 percent to 18.92 billion Belgian francs, with the share of Belgium and Western Europe falling to 56 from 62 percent in 1995, and the share of Asia and the Americas rising to 40 percent from 34 percent. Other regions accounted for an unchanged four percent.

Turnover rose in all the group's five divisions. Fastest growth was in cable television and satellite systems, although "communications" remains the second smallest with turnover of 1.62 billion francs.

Turnover in the visualisation division (Barco's biggest), which makes specialised display and projection systems, rose 33 percent to 9.13 billion francs despite problems integrating two recently acquired U.S. companies American Video Communications Inc and Maya Video Communications Inc.

Turnover in automated systems rose 12 percent to 3.41 billion francs thanks mainly to a strong contribution from Swiss textiles machine company Loepfe AG, consolidated since 1995. Barco noted earnings in 1996 at its Belgian Elbicon unit, bought in September 1995, were still negative although the outlook for 1997 was positive.
Graphic systems turnover rose 14 percent to 4.00 billion francs. Turnover from other operations rose rose 15 percent to 764 million francs.
Vandamme added he expected no impact on Barco's share from the planned listing in June of the GIMV (Flemish regional investment company), Barco's biggest shareholder.

During 1996 GIMV cut its stake in Barco to 33.99 percent from 39.1 percent, following the end of a shareholder pact with Belgian holding company Asphales, which also reduced its stake to "under two percent" from 5.1 percent.
Vandamme said, however, the GIMV had reaffirmed it remained committed to remaining Barco's reference shareholder.
